extracted.intended_audience: NIH SBIR/STTR reviewers and Phase II applicants; project teams and biomedical/drug-development stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A Phase II STTR/ SBIR research plan and commercialization strategy for lead optimization and pre-IND candidate selection of broad‑spectrum antiviral small molecules, including required PHS 398 form sections and experimental/ADME/PK safety criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Property Management Agreement (IPMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: FCCDC and the University of Pennsylvania have negotiated and signed an Intellectual Property Management Agreement (IPMA) to codify the terms of distributions of milestones and royalties from this project, and to establish the mechanisms for project governance and patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement/expectation that an IP agreement be in place to govern milestone/royalty distributions, project governance, and patent protection prior to commercialization or licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization / Revenue Stream expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: A primary source of revenue for this program will most likely be from licensure to the US government and the Department of Defense. A licensing deal would generate income through a combination of upfront fees, milestone payments and royalties on production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal should present plausible revenue pathways (e.g., government/DoD licensure, out-licensing, sale), precedent examples (e.g., tecovirimat/BARDA awards), and a staffing/BD plan to manage commercial relationships. Discuss alternate paths (subcontract manufacturing, pursue grants/pre-seed investments) and note pre-seed/seed investments are working capital, not revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglected Disease Priority Review Voucher as value driver
rubrics_metrics.description: The major source of revenue anticipated for this program is the Neglected Disease Priority Review Voucher offered by the U.S. FDA for new agents to treat neglected diseases such as Marburg, Ebola; this voucher could be sold to a pharmaceutical company for cash considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, proposals should identify eligibility for regulatory incentives (priority review vouchers) and quantify potential value as part of commercialization rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Vertebrate Animals Section – euthanasia & AVMA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Are vertebrate animals euthanized? If 'Yes' — Is the method consistent with American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA) guidelines? If not, describe method and provide scientific justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications involving vertebrate animals must explicitly state euthanasia plans and confirm AVMA guideline consistency or provide justification for deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Program Income reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: *Is program income anticipated during the periods for which the grant support is requested? If 'Yes' then use specified format to list Budget Period, Anticipated Amount ($), Source(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If program income is expected, provide a budgeted schedule of amounts and sources per budget period; otherwise leave blank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Embryonic Stem Cells (hESC) disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: *Does the proposed project involve human embryonic stem cells? If yes, list registration numbers from the NIH registry or indicate that one from the registry will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects involving hESC must list specific registered cell line numbers or assert future use of a registry-listed line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Fetal Tissue (HFT) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: *Does the proposed project involve human fetal tissue obtained from elective abortions? If 'yes' then provide the HFT Compliance Assurance and HFT Sample IRB Consent Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any use of human fetal tissue requires explicit regulatory/IRB documentation/assurances to be provided with the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions and Patents reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: *Inventions and Patents: indicate Yes/No. If Yes, indicate whether previously reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal applications must disclose inventions and patents and prior reporting status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Change (Change of PI/Institution) reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Change of Project Director/Principal Investigator or Change of Grantee Institution sections require naming former PD/PI or former institution when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When key personnel or institutional changes occur, include full prior information as required by PHS forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of Required Research Plan Sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Plan must include: Specific Aims; Research Strategy; Progress Report Publication List; Vertebrate Animals; Select Agent Research; Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan; Consortium/Contractual Arrangements; Letters of Support; Resource Sharing Plans; Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources; Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all listed Research Plan subsections and appendices are included and appropriately labeled/attached in submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims clarity and goal statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims should state the ultimate goal (here: discover and develop novel small molecule, broad-spectrum therapeutics against viral infections that depend on PPxY L-domain motif) and list explicit aims (lead optimization; evaluate ability to inhibit PPxY-mediated egress; in vitro/in vivo ADMET evaluation; analysis against authentic hemorrhagic fever viruses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims must be specific, feasible, and tied to an overarching translational goal (e.g., selecting predevelopment candidates for IND enabling studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance and Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the unmet need, public health importance, and how the proposed approach addresses the need (e.g., no existing small molecule therapeutics; host-oriented inhibitors may reduce drug resistance and be broad-spectrum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how success would change current paradigms, clinical practice, or public health preparedness; include rationale and potential use cases (treatment, prophylaxis for high-risk personnel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight conceptual and technical innovations (e.g., host-oriented broad-spectrum inhibitors, VLP budding assays under BSL-2, use of VSV recombinants as BSL-2 surrogates, novel medicinal chemistry series, patent coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how approaches or technologies differ from/advance beyond existing work; provide concrete examples of methodological innovation and translational novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Data / Progress to Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide prior work and findings that support feasibility (SAR, proof-of-concept in mouse model, published manuscripts, patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quantitative preliminary results that justify aims (e.g., in vivo proof of concept, number of compounds synthesized, prior efficacy data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Team expertise and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine pharmaceutical/medicinal chemistry expertise (FCCDC) with virology expertise (Harty Lab) and BSL-4 evaluation capability (Shtanko lab).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate complementary expertise, prior collaboration history, and access to necessary facilities (BSL-4) and personnel to accomplish aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental rigor and statistical validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that all assay experiments will be completed in a rigorous, unbiased manner, and quantitative readouts from virological assays will be statistically validated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for appropriate controls, blinding when feasible, replication, and pre-specified statistical analyses for quantitative endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 1: Lead optimization medicinal chemistry criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop FC-10696 analogs to increase solubility and improve potency, ADME, PK and safety properties suitable for once-daily oral dosing; perform SAR lead diversification using cutting edge medicinal chemistry methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterative design/synthesis informed by ADME/PK data; target properties include improved aqueous solubility, metabolic stability, oral bioavailability and potency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 2: Biological evaluation / selectivity criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether new compounds block PPxY-mediated budding of VLPs (EBOV/MARV VP40 and LAFV Z proteins) using budding assays and a bimolecular Nedd4:PPxY complementation (BiMC) approach; evaluate effects on Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination and ESCRT-associated functions; use RNA-seq to assess host transcriptome/off-target effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use orthogonal assays (VLP budding, BiMC, ubiquitination assays, transcriptomics) to demonstrate mechanism-specific inhibition and identify potential off-target consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 3: ADMET and PK evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate up to 15 compounds/year in vitro for microsomal stability, CYP3A4 inhibition, solubility, plasma protein binding; evaluate 3–6 compounds in mouse PK (IV and PO); select 2–3 compounds for non-GLP safety assays (P450 isozyme inhibition panel, manual patch clamp hERG, Ames ± metabolic activation) and PK in rat, dog, and non-human primate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish throughput and decision gates (number of compounds, in vitro thresholds) and perform cross-species PK to inform candidate selection for in vivo testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 4: In vitro and in vivo efficacy against live BSL-4 pathogens
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate up to 4 compounds/year against live EBOV, MARV, LASV in human cell cultures; use a mouse model to assess toxicity, body distribution and accumulation; evaluate two lead compounds/year for antiviral efficacy in mouse challenge models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance only compounds meeting in vitro potency and ADME/PK criteria to BSL-4 testing; use well-characterized animal challenge models to demonstrate efficacy and tolerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead candidate selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Select compounds that meet in vitro potency and ADME/PK criteria, show acceptable safety in non-GLP assays, have favorable PK (e.g., good stability in human liver microsomes, acceptable bioavailability), and low risk for drug–drug interactions (e.g., do not inhibit CYP3A4 at concentrations up to 33 µM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a tiered selection pipeline (Aim 1→Aim 2→Aim 3→Aim 4) with explicit cutoffs (e.g., CYP inhibition thresholds, microsomal stability, PK exposure metrics) to nominate predevelopment candidates for IND enabling studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of BSL-2 surrogates prior to BSL-4 work
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovative use of VSV and VSV recombinants (e.g., VSV-M40) as surrogate viruses for BSL-4 pathogens to test inhibitors under BSL-2 conditions prior to BSL-4 experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ validated surrogate systems to screen compounds and reduce risk/cost before conducting high-containment studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicinal chemistry SAR design principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve metabolic stability and solubility by modifying the acylurea side chain and quinoxaline scaffold (e.g., prepare compounds with covalent six‑membered rings, create biphenyl and thiazole benzyl subseries, replace quinoxaline with sulfur-containing side chains to retain potency and improve microsomal stability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rational SAR modifications should be justified by structural/chemical reasoning (e.g., internal H-bonding, pseudo six-membered ring conformation) and supported by in vitro stability and potency data.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADME/PK experimental metrics and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report mouse PK metrics (IP bioavailability %, AUC, Cmax, t1/2), microsomal stability (MLM, HLM), Log D, TPSA, and report % VLP reduction at tested concentrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tabulated in vitro/in vivo ADME and PK data for selected compounds and use these quantitative metrics to compare compounds and justify advancement to efficacy studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bench assay quantitation and data presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify VLP and VP40/eVP40 levels using NIH Image-J software; report '% of VLP after compound treatment relative to DMSO control set at 100%'; perform Western blots at specified timepoints (e.g., 24 hours post‑transfection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt standard image analysis and normalized reporting conventions; include representative blots/figures and clearly state experimental conditions/timepoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of compounds for live-virus and mouse efficacy experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Compounds with good stability to human liver microsomes and no CYP3A4 inhibition up to 33 µM were deemed suitable for live virus and mouse efficacy experiments; FC-10696 had superior PK properties among tested analogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both metabolic stability (HLM/MLM) and CYP inhibition data as gating criteria before proceeding to live-virus animal studies; highlight top candidates with superior combined profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation & appendices (e.g., resource sharing, authentication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Resource Sharing Plan(s), Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources, Letters of Support, Consortium/Contractual Arrangements, and Appendix materials as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required institutional and resource-authentication documentation and supporting letters to strengthen feasibility and reproducibility claims.
